meta.title: TU/e Digital Exhibition — WordPress & App Recap
meta.subtitle: Where the WordPress site and the new Nuxt application stand, what we are waiting for, and how the pieces fit together
meta.client: TU/e — Built Environment, Digital Exhibition platform
meta.author: marco@tech-paw.com
meta.scope: The app runs on the TU/e server (linux3) and reads the live WordPress. The two addresses have not been switched yet.

tldr: The WordPress code of staging has been merged into live (staging's version won). Both sites now follow the same branch, and their databases stay separate. Staging keeps using the Cloudflare R2 bucket for images, for development only; live keeps all its images on its own server.

The new front-end is a Nuxt application. It no longer runs on Cloudflare: it runs on the TU/e server (linux3) at live.digitalexhibition.arch.tue.nl and reads the live WordPress. GitHub builds it and linux3 only downloads the finished files. The Cloudflare address stays as a preview.
The Deploy Frontend button in WordPress now does the whole job: it starts the build on GitHub, then asks linux3 to download the result. Nobody has to log in to the server to publish a change.

Still to do: switch the two addresses (the app takes digitalexhibition.arch.tue.nl, WordPress live moves to live.digitalexhibition.arch.tue.nl), run the search and replace in the database, and fix the email on WordPress and on the app. The email waits for TU/e to fix the Microsoft mail.

actions.title: Email system
actions.detail: Password reset and the contact form need a working mail service. WordPress live has FluentSMTP installed, ready to connect to TU/e's Microsoft mail as soon as it works. The contact form of the app checks the message but sends nothing yet: its mail connection is not finished, so it needs the same sender. Brevo (free plan, 300 emails per day) is the alternative.
actions.ask: Fix the Microsoft mail, so the sender can be set up in FluentSMTP and in the app.

actions.title: Switch the addresses and update the database
actions.detail: The app takes digitalexhibition.arch.tue.nl and WordPress live moves to live.digitalexhibition.arch.tue.nl. Every address stored in the WordPress database is replaced (search and replace, after a backup), the app is pointed at the new WordPress address.
actions.ask: Planned after this update, at a quiet moment. Nothing is needed from TU/e for the content itself.

actions.title: Tests before going live
actions.detail: Most parts have already been tested. After the address switch the application gets a final check on desktop and mobile, including the forms. On WordPress, the new admin UX/UI gets manual and automated testing.
actions.ask: Manual and automated testing of the new WordPress interface, after the switch.

actions.title: Hosting decided: linux3
actions.detail: The app runs on the TU/e server (linux3) instead of Cloudflare, so the question about Cloudflare or another host (such as Bunny.net) is closed. The Cloudflare address stays as a preview, and the R2 bucket is kept for staging only.

actions.title: Staging merged into live
actions.detail: The files of staging were merged into live (staging's version won). The databases were not merged: live's database is only changed by running prepared scripts. Host files and live-only plugins were left as they are.

plugins.name: Figuro Folders
plugins.does: Media library folders. It replaces FileBird Pro; the folders and files were imported from FileBird (438 folders, 3,943 files in the latest import).

plugins.name: SVG Support
plugins.does: Allows SVG uploads such as logos and other vector images.

plugins.name: Advanced Media Offloader
plugins.does: Sends uploads to the Cloudflare R2 bucket. It is active on staging only, for development; live keeps its files local.

plugins.name: Activity Log
plugins.does: Records who changed what in the WordPress admin.

plugins.name: Frontend Deploy
plugins.does: The “Deploy Frontend” button. Editors write their pages, then press it once: it starts the build on GitHub and asks linux3 to download the result, so no one needs to touch the server. Renamed from Cloudflare Deploy Trigger; all Cloudflare code was removed.

environments.title: Test new features
environments.text: Try changes on the WordPress site before they reach the live site.

environments.title: Emergency replica
environments.text: If something goes wrong, staging can copy the live environment to reproduce and find errors.

environments.title: Cloudflare R2 for images
environments.text: Staging reads its images from the R2 bucket. This is for development only; live does not use it.

email.title: Where the email stands
email.text: WordPress live will send its mail through FluentSMTP, connected to TU/e's Microsoft mail once that is fixed. The app's contact form does not send mail yet: it is prepared for Brevo but the connection is not finished, so it needs a decision too. A single sender for both would be simplest. Brevo (300 emails per day on its free plan) is still the alternative.

before.label: WordPress live — files on its own server

afterNotes: Live does not use R2: every image and PDF stays on its own server.
The staging uploads folder was deleted, so staging reads only from the R2 bucket.
The R2 settings exist only in staging's configuration, so the code shared with live does nothing with R2 there.

postmortem.title: Post-mortem — the theme update that broke the front-end
postmortem.summary: WordPress updated the site's theme by itself and replaced our files with a different theme. That broke the layout of the WordPress site. We renamed the theme, so it is no longer connected to the WordPress theme repository and this cannot happen again. The theme is now called tue-digital-exhibition, a name that does not exist in the WordPress repository (not automatic download anymore).

chain.label: Automatic update
chain.text: WordPress updated the theme on its own.

chain.label: Files replaced
chain.text: The theme had no child theme, so the update replaced it completely with files from the WordPress theme repository.

chain.label: Layout broken
chain.text: The WordPress front-end design stopped working.

chain.label: Theme renamed
chain.text: The theme is now called tue-digital-exhibition, which is not in the WordPress theme repository, so no update can overwrite it.

changesIntro: The staging code was merged into live, so both WordPress sites now run the same code. They still differ in their environment: staging uses the Cloudflare R2 bucket for images, live keeps its images locally, and live has its own plugins (such as FluentSMTP). The databases are separate.

discovery.summary: Within the hosting platform (Flask) we found a web application firewall. Sometimes it made the deployment of the app hard, because it blocked requests that our development and deployment need.

modes.label: Staging
modes.text: The firewall is on and blocks what it considers a risk. This is the setting that got in our way.

modes.label: Live website
modes.text: The firewall only records what it would block. It blocks nothing.

discovery.did: For development we added security rule ID 210580 to the firewall settings, so that it no longer blocks our work.
discovery.optionsTitle: The three ways to handle it

options.title: Keep the exception
options.text: The firewall stays on and rule 210580 is added to its settings. This is what we do now.

options.title: Switch it off
options.text: The firewall stops filtering requests altogether.

options.title: Detection only
options.text: Like the live website: it records suspicious requests but never blocks them.
